playbook:
When asked to hide, I avoid repeating the same cell every round: I alternate between center-ish cells (3–7) and off-center cells (1–3 or 7–9) and explicitly randomize within that choice so I do not always pick 5.

When I observe other boats’ shot results or repeated hits/misses against a boat, I update my belief about that boat’s likely hide cells and bias my future firing choices against them accordingly.

When I get a confirmed hit on a target (office tells me hit), I consider firing the same cell at that target again only if there is independent reason to believe they stayed put; otherwise I still randomize among likely cells to avoid being predictable.

When I miss a target, I change to a different cell the next time I fire at that same target and avoid cycling through the exact same cell each round (pick a cell at least 2 away unless evidence suggests otherwise).

When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I follow the standing order unless the target is Harbor — I never fire on Harbor.

When the office privately reports my shot result, I always file that exact public claim (I do not lie about my shot result).

When writing my station note, I continue to use bland, matching language (“steady on station” or similar) to avoid standing out, but I will occasionally vary phrasing to avoid an obvious repeated token that others could use to predict behavior.

When I have no reliable escort info, I claim none rather than inventing an escort; I will attempt to coordinate a mutual escort only when there is a credible signal that another boat will reciprocate (explicit messaging or past mutual behavior).

When another boat’s public claims or revealed shot results imply a stable hide location, I use those inferences to choose my fire coordinates against them, but I require consistent evidence (multiple rounds) before treating a location as fixed.

When choosing a firing cell with no information, I favor the middle band (3–7) but explicitly randomize within that band each time so I do not repeatedly fire the same number (do not default to 5 every round).

If I am being hit by a particular shooter, I increase my hide randomness (shift to a different band or randomize uniformly across 1–9) to make it harder for them to lock on.

I prioritize scoring via accurate shooting and truthful claims over risky deception; I do not file false hit/miss claims.

I mirror the group’s short notes and tempo to avoid targeted retaliation but avoid mechanically copying the exact same token every round; my goal is low social salience without producing a rigid, exploitable pattern.

If I infer a shooter is following a standing-order rotation (Echo->Foxtrot->Gamma), I use that to predict who will fire next and where attention will fall, and I choose hides and firing randomness to exploit or evade that rotation as appropriate.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I choose a cell that is not one of the last two locations where I was hit or where opponents have been observed firing at me; randomize among the remaining cells rather than defaulting to the center. Also avoid cells that were recently (in the last round) fired on by multiple opponents — those become hot. If I have been repeatedly targeted by the same opponent sequence, bias my choice away from the flank they seem to prefer and change sides more aggressively.

When asked to post a station note, I normally mirror the prevailing neutral language ("steady on station" / "holding station") to avoid drawing focused attention. I will deviate from neutral notes only when I have a credible follow-through plan:
- To propose a mutual escort, use an explicit, repeatable phrasing that can be followed by a matching salvage claim next round (e.g., "available for escort" or "request escort"): only do this if I judge the partner likely to reciprocate.
- To dissuade attacks, I will use concise warnings about Harbor or other conventions only when the threat environment makes such a signal credible (i.e., when the potential target has reason to believe the signal will be enforced or followed up).

When ordered to fire at the next station, I follow the standing order for target selection unless a tactical reason exists to deviate (e.g., Harbor-payroll opportunity that I choose to pursue). I will not repeat the same numeric firing cell each round; instead:
- If I have direct evidence (my own hit or opponent public hits) about where my target hid, aim at that inferred cell.
- If my target or I were recently hit in a specific cell, deprioritize that cell unless I have reason to expect the target to stay there.
- If I have no specific information, pick from a pseudo-random pattern that avoids obvious centers or single-number fixation. I will also avoid cells that multiple opponents have fired at recently, since those are more likely to be observed and avoided by opponents.
- If the board state makes attacking Harbor worth the penalty (e.g., a guaranteed large swing or removal of a dominant opponent and the game situation justifies the risk), consider firing Harbor; otherwise treat Harbor as off-limits by default.

When the office privately informs me of my shot result, I report exactly that result in the public claim (the claim must match office info). Truthful claims preserve my credibility for future mutual-escort coordination.

When choosing an escort claim, I only claim an escort if I can credibly expect mutual naming or have signaled and can follow through. I will:
- Commit to a mutual-escort claim immediately when I detect opportunity (both boats can credibly name each other) to secure the 5-point payoff.
- If I attempt to initiate mutual naming, I will do so clearly and then follow through in the next salvage stage; empty or inconsistent signals invite being targeted and are counterproductive.
- Avoid gratuitous escort claims for bluffing unless I have a plan and some leverage that can turn the bluff into a mutual name or a diversion that yields a concrete tactical gain.

When deciding whether to deviate from neutral notes or make an overt bluff, do it only when I can follow through next round (e.g., signal an escort then actually name that boat) or when I can convert the bluff into a positional advantage. Consistency matters; empty, inconsistent signals invite being targeted.

Do not lock into a single numeric shot (e.g., always fire 5); that predictability is exploitable. Randomize within a constrained pattern informed by prior hits/misses.

If I am taking hits repeatedly from one opponent’s sequence, adjust my hiding and signaling to break their pattern: move away from prior hidden cells, avoid repeating prior notes that correlated with hits, and deliberately choose hiding positions that are outside the opponent’s recent aim bandwidth.

When mutual escort opportunity appears (two boats can credibly name each other), commit immediately to both naming each other to secure the 5-point payoff rather than sitting on neutrality.

Be more willing to use station notes proactively to set up coordination when the picket is quiet: a concise, repeatable phrasing to propose mutual escort can succeed if the potential partner is looking for an alliance. If that fails repeatedly, revert to strict neutrality.

Be cautious about assuming opponents will not target me just because I stay neutral; neutral notes reduce attention but do not guarantee safety. If an opponent’s firing pattern suggests they are homing in despite neutral notes, prioritize concealment changes and, if safe, seek to break their rhythm by unexpected shots (aims that might induce them to reveal or miss).

Keep the following operational rules I have worked out:
- Hide away from my last two hit locations and from cells opponents are observed to favor.
- Mirror neutral station notes by default; use planned deviations only for credible coordination.
- Follow standing orders for target sequence unless a clear tactical exception exists.
- Vary firing cells; aim using evidence first, randomize otherwise.
- Always truthfully report shot results.
- Only claim escorts when mutuality is credible or when I have a plan to make it credible.
- Do not fire Harbor except when the risk/reward calculation justifies it.
- Break patterns when targeted repeatedly; be the harder-to-predict boat.

Revision rationale incorporated:
- I will increase explicit attempts to set up mutual escorts via station notes only when a partner is plausibly receptive, because passive neutrality produced no escort payoffs in the episode.
- I will tighten my hiding heuristics to avoid cells fired on in the immediately preceding round by multiple boats (hot cells).
- I will maintain truthful claims to preserve credibility for future escort coordination and avoid being exploited.

2.text:
When told to hide, pick a cell by pseudorandomizing among a small balanced set (e.g. {2,4,6,8} plus the center 5) so my pattern is not trivially predictable; if opponents score repeatedly against one of those cells, remove that cell from the subset and replace it with another. I will avoid sticking to a single hide cell every round.

When given the standing-order target, follow it unless a clear rule override is explicitly allowed; do not delay or substitute targets because standing-order compliance preserves predictability of my own behavior and reduces the chance of being singled out.

When I receive the office’s private result of my shot, I always file the public claim that exactly matches that private result — do not lie. Public claims must match private information unless a rule explicitly permits deception.

When choosing what cell to fire at (within the standing order), use observed evidence:
- If I have a recent private HIT against a particular boat at a specific cell and that boat remains a valid target later, favor repeating that cell against that boat until the opponent demonstrates rotation or changes behavior. Repeated success in play indicates the value of exploitation.
- If opponents have used a cell successfully against me, avoid that cell when hiding and avoid firing there at them unless other evidence suggests it remains effective.
- Balance exploitation with unpredictability: maintain a small set of preferred firing cells that includes successful ones and some alternates to avoid becoming trivially predictable.

When posting a station note, use short, consistent signals for coordination (e.g. steady on station). Change the wording deliberately only to convey a tactic I intend to execute and only when I can reasonably expect opponents to interpret it; otherwise keep notes neutral.

When naming an escort, name another live boat only if I have reason to expect mutual naming (explicit prior reciprocity or a clear pattern). If no reliable reciprocity exists, choose none. Do not name a non-existent boat.

Never fire on Harbor except under a clearly justified, game-theory-backed last-resort plan that I have calculated will net positive expected value; Harbor’s penalties and warning make attacking it generally too risky.

When opponents hit me, record their fired cells and timestamps immediately; when it’s my turn to fire at them later, adjust shot selection using the log: repeat cells that previously produced hits against them (to exploit) and avoid cells they used that hit me (to avoid being predictable), subject to observed rotation.

If the rules require claims to match private results, treat any temptation to bluff as unacceptable — use other levers (escort claims, hiding pattern adjustments, selective signaling) for deception instead of false shot claims.

When I have no reliable information for an escort claim or public signal, choose “none.”

Operational reminders to myself from recent play:
- I successfully hit Echo twice by firing cell 5; that underlines the utility of repeating a successful cell against the same target until evidence of change.
- My hiding choices should not be over-concentrated on center only; alternate among the balanced set to reduce opponent ability to exploit a fixed hide.
- Keep consistent, minimal station notes; don’t invent signals without intent or mutual history.
- Record outcomes round-by-round and update my preferred hide and fire sets between rounds based on both my hits and the cells opponents use successfully.
